title: Anthropic launches roadshow for an IPO that could raise $64.4 billion at a $1 trillion-plus valuation
excerpt: AI lab Anthropic has launched the roadshow for an initial public offering that could raise up to $64.4 billion, targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion — or $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
content:
Artificial intelligence lab Anthropic has launched the roadshow for an initial public offering that could raise up to $64.4 billion — one of the largest share sales ever — targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion, according to a draft prospectus disclosed Nov. 10 and reported by Reuters.

The company and some of its investors plan to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 per share. On a fully diluted basis — including stock options and restricted stock — the company would be worth up to $1.4 trillion. That is below the roughly $2 trillion valuation figure that circulated over the summer.

Anthropic will also raise $26 billion in a separate private placement with cornerstone investors including Alphabet's Google, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the IPO.

Reuters describes the listing as a key test of Wall Street's faith in the AI boom, amid growing worries about the risks of the massive spending behind it.

For readers here, the listing is a bellwether for the AI buildout — including the data centers and power demand Texas is debating — rather than a local event. Webb Watch covered Gov. Abbott's data-center pause in October; the Anthropic numbers show the capital still flowing into AI even as that debate continues.

Sources: Reuters, Nov. 10, 2026.
